B2c-01-food-classes-chart

Chart of the classes of food arranged as seven coloured circles around a central plate. Each circle holds a simple drawing of typical Nigerian foods: carbohydrates (yam tuber, garri, rice, bread), proteins (beans, egg, fish, meat), fats and oils (bottle of red palm oil, groundnuts, butter), vitamins (orange, carrot, green ugwu leaves), mineral salts (salt shaker, milk, crayfish), water (glass of water), roughage (okro, whole fruits, vegetables). Soft pastel colours, each class in a different colour.
B2c-02-carbohydrate-molecular-schematic

Simple diagram showing carbohydrate building blocks as coloured hexagons. Top row: a single hexagon labelled monosaccharide (glucose). Middle row: two hexagons joined, labelled disaccharide (maltose), with an arrow showing water removed (condensation) and an arrow back showing water added (hydrolysis). Bottom row: a long chain of many hexagons labelled polysaccharide (starch), and a branched chain labelled glycogen.
B2c-03-triglyceride-hydrolysis-schematic

Simple diagram of a triglyceride (fat) molecule: a short vertical bar on the left labelled glycerol, with three long zig-zag tails coming off it to the right, each labelled fatty acid. Below, an arrow labelled hydrolysis (digestion by lipase) points to the separated glycerol and three fatty acids.
B2c-04-vitamin-classification-infographic

Two-column chart of vitamins. Left column headed fat-soluble with four yellow oil-drop icons labelled A, D, E, K, each with a small food picture (A: carrot and red palm oil; D: sun and egg; E: vegetable oil bottle; K: green leaves). Right column headed water-soluble with blue water-drop icons labelled B1, B2, B3, B12, C, each with a small food picture (B1: unpolished rice and beans; B2: milk and egg; B3: groundnuts and meat; B12: liver and fish; C: orange and guava).
B2c-05-food-groups-market-display

Illustrated market-stall style chart of Nigerian food sources grouped into labelled baskets. Basket 1: yam, cassava, garri, rice, maize, plantain. Basket 2: beans, eggs, fish, crayfish, meat, milk. Basket 3: red palm oil bottle, groundnuts, coconut, shea butter. Basket 4: oranges, guava, carrots, mango, pawpaw. Basket 5: green ugwu leaves, efo (spinach), okro, garden egg. Basket 6: glass of water and a watermelon slice. Warm soft colours.
B2c-06-food-energy-calorimetry-apparatus

Laboratory set-up for measuring the energy in food: a clamp stand holding a boiling tube containing water with a thermometer in it; below the tube, a burning groundnut on the tip of a mounted needle held in a cork. A Bunsen burner sits to one side.
B2c-08-rickets-skeletal

Simple medical illustration comparing the legs of a healthy child (straight leg bones) with a child with rickets (bow legs curving outwards), shown standing side by side from the front, with the leg bones drawn faintly visible inside the outline.
B2c-09-goitre-medical

Simple medical illustration of an adult woman's head and neck from the front showing a large rounded swelling at the front of the lower neck (goitre), with a small inset diagram showing the position of the butterfly-shaped thyroid gland on the windpipe.
B2c-10-balanced-diet-plate

A balanced diet plate divided into sections, viewed from above, with Nigerian foods: about one third vegetables and fruits (ugwu leaves, tomatoes, carrots, orange slices, pawpaw), about one third starchy foods (jollof rice, boiled yam, plantain), a smaller section of protein foods (fried fish, boiled egg, beans, chicken), a small section of milk and dairy (glass of milk, wara), a tiny section of fats and oils (small bottle of palm oil). A glass of water beside the plate.
B2c-11-iodine-starch-test-tile

Iodine test for starch on a white spotting tile: a dropper adding brown iodine solution to three wells. The first well contains crushed yam and has turned blue-black, the second contains sugar solution and stays yellow-brown, the third contains distilled water as a control and stays yellow-brown. A small brown bottle of iodine solution stands beside the tile.
B2c-15-salivary-amylase-digestion-experiment

Experiment on starch digestion by saliva: two test tubes labelled A and B standing in a water bath at 37 °C with a thermometer. Tube A contains starch solution and saliva; tube B contains starch solution and boiled saliva. Below each tube, two small results tubes: for A, iodine test yellow-brown and Benedict's test brick-red; for B, iodine test blue-black and Benedict's test blue.
B2c-12-benedicts-reducing-sugar-test

Benedict's test for reducing sugar: a beaker of boiling water (water bath) on a tripod over a Bunsen burner, holding a test tube with food solution and Benedict's solution. Beside it, a row of five test tubes showing the colour sequence from blue, green, yellow, orange to brick-red precipitate at the bottom.
B2c-13-protein-biuret-millons-tests

Two protein tests side by side. Left: Biuret test, a test tube with egg white solution after adding sodium hydroxide and copper(II) sulphate, showing a violet (purple) colour, next to a control tube of distilled water that stays blue; a dropper bottle labelled copper sulphate beside them. Right: Millon's test, a test tube in a warm water bath showing a brick-red precipitate.
B2c-14-lipid-food-tests-results

Three tests for fats and oils in a row. Left: Sudan III test, a test tube with a red-stained oil layer floating on top of colourless water. Middle: grease-spot test, a piece of white filter paper held up to light with a translucent spot from groundnut and a dry, opaque area where water was placed as a control. Right: emulsion test, a test tube of water turned cloudy white after adding ethanol containing dissolved oil, next to a clear control tube.
